text:
Mira (Marketing): quick, non-blocking ask for launch docs — we need a reproducible bench that proves provenance + warmup protocol effects. 10k stratified samples. slices: <32, 32-256, 256-1024, >1024. langs: en, es, zh, ar, other. variants: rwd-7b-v1 (fp32) and rwd-7b-q4_0_v2. deliver: per-slice p50/p90/p99, token-cost, failure-rate, prompt-length CDF, and raw traces. also include a small metadata file with sample provenance (query + sample_ids) so marketing can trace claims back to origins. seed=31415. can we get commands + artifacts by Thu morning?

Cade (Runtime): we can run this. couple clarifying items: 1) provenance: do you want full sample_ids list + the SQL used to pick them? 2) warmup: separate warm vs cold? if yes, how do you want them tagged? 3) routing: prod mix or enforced per-lang minima?

Mira (Marketing): yes to full sample_ids and the exact SQL. separate warm/cold please 1 warmup_tokens=4 and tag warm requests with header X-Bench-Warm=1. use production routing mix but enforce min 1k per language. include concurrency sweep 4/8. keep extreme sequences capped at 8192.

Ilya (Eng): FYI >1024 will exercise a different kernel path; recommend logging kernel_path and kernel_fallback_count. if zh shows concentrated failures, we should run a small follow-up with zh warmup_tokens=12. also include a tiny reproducibility note: runtime will save RNG state + seed in artifact metadata.

Mira (Marketing): great. provenance must include: SQL, rand_seed, any pre-filters, and the exact timestamp of extraction. we want that in a single provenance.txt in the artifacts.

Nico (Ops): i'll queue a low-priority job on staging at 04:30 UTC tomorrow. example run command i'll execute:

./run_bench --model=rwd-7b-v1 --quant=fp32 --samples=10000 \ 
  --buckets "<32,32-256,256-1024,>1024" --langs "en,es,zh,ar,other" \ 
  --min_per_lang 1000 --warmup_tokens 4 --warm_header "X-Bench-Warm=1" \ 
  --concurrency 8 --batch 32 --cap 8192 --seed 31415 \ 
  --provenance_sql "/mnt/marketing/select_provenance.sql" --tag=bench-provenance

and the same for rwd-7b-q4_0_v2 with --quant=q4_0. i'll post job id when queued. :thumbsup:

benchbot: Job queued -> jb-20260401-550. est runtime ~4h. logs: https://ci/internal/jb-20260401-550/logs

Cade (Runtime): implementation note: per-request CSV will have: req_id, sample_id, seed, lang, token_count, warm_flag, latency_ms, token_cost, error_code, kernel_path. provenance.txt will contain SQL, extraction_ts, rand_seed, and list of sample_ids (CSV). good?

Mira (Marketing): perfect. please also include a tiny README.md in the artifacts with the exact run commands used and the job id. we'll link to that from the launch doc.

benchbot: jb-20260401-550 finished. artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/marketing/4799998888/. short first-pass: q4_0_v2 shows ~7% lower p50 on <32 but a ~10% p99 regression on >1024. failure rate 0.22% overall, concentrated in long zh examples. provenance.txt, per-slice CSVs, prompt-length CDF, raw traces, and README.md are in the bucket.

Ilya (Eng): saw ~18 kernel_fallback_count entries for zh tokenization. stacks serialized to the bucket. recommend a focused zh warmup_tokens=12 follow-up before we finalize any public claims.

Mira (Marketing): thanks everyone  this is exactly the chain-of-custody and bench detail we need for the press + webinar. we'll review and circle back if we want the zh follow-up. :sparkles:
